title: OxyGen: Unified KV Cache Management for VLA Inference under Multi-Task Parallelism
claim: Existing systems recompute and contend for resources across concurrent tasks; sharing one cache across tasks and frames removes this and speeds inference.
layout: 2 panels: left example timeline, right stacked isolated-vs-unified comparison, top-to-bottom
description: The left panel shows a robot control timeline with three frames (t-2, t-1, t), each a kitchen camera photo. The frames feed a wide 'MoT VLA Inference: Actions + Language' bar. Arrows lead down to per-frame action boxes with robot-arm icons, and to a gray box of language memory text. The right panel is a rounded box with a big arrow pointing into it. Its top half is titled 'Isolated KV (existing)' in red. It shows a timeline of colored VLM, Act. and Lang. blocks, with Act. KV and Lang. KV boxes, and braces labeled 'Resource contention' and 'Recompute'. A dashed line separates it from the bottom half, 'Unified KV (ours)' in green. That half shows a compact timeline sitting on a 'Unified KV cache manager' bar. It carries a '3.7× speedup' badge and red-to-green numbers for action frequency and language throughput.
caption: Left: An example of deploying a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model for parallel multi-task inference: from per-frame observations, the VLA generates robot actions within each frame while continuously generating language-based memories across frames [ref]. Right: Comparison between paradigms of MoT VLA inference: existing systems manage the KV cache in isolation, slowing down inference through redundant computation and resource contention; our method adopts unified KV cache management, achieving up to 3.7$\times$ speedup via cross-task KV sharing and cross-frame continuous batching.
abstract: Embodied AI agents increasingly require parallel execution of multiple tasks, such as manipulation, conversation, and memory construction, from shared observations under distinct time constraints. Recent Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) support such heterogeneous outputs, yet existing inference systems incur redundant computation and resource contention when serving concurrent tasks on-device. We identify isolated KV cache management as the root cause. To address this, we propose unified KV cache management, an inference design that treats the KV cache as a first-class shared resource across tasks and control cycles. This abstraction enables two key optimizations: cross-task KV sharing eliminates redundant prefill of shared observations, while cross-frame continuous batching batches unfinished language requests from different frames and advances them within a per-frame decoding budget. We implement this design in OxyGen and evaluate $Ï_{0.5}$ on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Thor. OxyGen achieves up to 3.7$\times$ speedup over isolated execution, delivering over 200 tokens/s language throughput and 70 Hz action frequency simultaneously on RTX 4090. We also validate the design on Xiaomi-Robotics-0 and StarVLA across different backbones and expert configurations. We further demonstrate the inference gains on a humanoid robot with on-board Jetson AGX Thor.
